owner.title: Home Assistant owner
owner.description: Signed in to Ezlo as {email}. Choose the Home Assistant user that your own devices and Ezlo cloud services act as.

http.title: Show real client IPs
http.description: QuicHarc reaches Home Assistant over loopback. So that Home Assistant sees the real IP address of web visitors (for IP bans, login notifications and logs), QuicHarc can turn on `use_x_forwarded_for` with `trusted_proxies: [127.0.0.1, ::1]` in Home Assistant's HTTP settings ({file}). Home Assistant applies HTTP settings when it restarts; QuicHarc checks the change works and keeps it, and Home Assistant undoes it by itself if it doesn't. Remote web access through Ezlo works once the change is in place.

agent_failed.title: QuicHarc agent isn't running
agent_failed.description: The QuicHarc agent isn't running: {error}. Remote access is unavailable until it runs.

agent_verify_failed.title: QuicHarc agent failed verification
agent_verify_failed.description: The downloaded QuicHarc agent didn't match its pinned hash or signature, so it wasn't run: {error}.

unsupported_arch.title: QuicHarc doesn't support this machine
unsupported_arch.description: There is no QuicHarc agent for the {arch} architecture. QuicHarc supports 64-bit x86 and ARM.

clock_skew.title: Home Assistant's clock is wrong
clock_skew.description: This host's clock is {skew} seconds off from the Ezlo cloud. QuicHarc's connection grants depend on time; fix the system time (for example with NTP).

subscription_lapsed.title: Ezlo remote access subscription ended
subscription_lapsed.description: Your Ezlo account had Home Assistant remote access, and it has ended. Renew the subscription to restore remote access. QuicHarc reconnects by itself within a few minutes of the renewal; there's nothing to change here.

identity_conflict.title: This home's identity is in use on another installation

init.title: Another installation took over remote access
init.description:
Another Home Assistant installation is running with this home's remote access identity, most likely a restored backup or a cloned machine. On {node} at {at} the Ezlo edge gave remote access to that installation, and this one stopped connecting so the two don't keep taking it from each other.

Use this installation: remote access moves back here, and the other installation gets this message instead. Leave it on the other one: nothing changes; this message is dismissed.

error.reclaim_failed: QuicHarc couldn't take remote access back. Check that the agent is running and try again.

abort.conflict_gone: This installation already has remote access.
abort.left_on_other: Remote access stays with the other installation.

subscription_required.title: Ezlo remote access needs a subscription
subscription_required.description: Your Ezlo account doesn't include Home Assistant remote access. Remote access through Ezlo needs a subscription on this account. Once the account has it, QuicHarc connects by itself within a few minutes; there's nothing to change here.
